To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have identified and characterized a cell-permeant p53 COOH-terminus peptide (p53p) which induces apoptosis in human and rodent glioma cells, and that the peptide can be successfully delivered into a rat brain tumor by convection-enhanced intratumoral infusion.

we have shown that a p53 COH-terminal peptide linked to the truncated Ant homeobox domain as a carrier for cellular transduction induces rapid apoptosis selectively in human and rat malignant glioma cells, which contain endogenous mutant pcls or wild-type p53, but not in nonmalignanr human and rat glia or normal human peripheral marrow cells, which contain WT p53.

a peptide derived from the COOH-terminal regulatory region of the p53 tumor suppressor protein, when linked to the truncated Antennapedia homeobox domain as a carrier for cell transduction, selectively induces apoptosis in human and animal malignant glioma cells, which contain endogenous p53 protein, in vitro and in an orthotopic rat glioma model in vivo, and that the mechanism for this selective apoptosis is by the activation of the Fas extracellular apoptotic pathway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies for the treatment of human gliomas, the most common and lethal of all primary brain tumors, which are resistant to conventional chemotherapy and radiation.
the development of a new class of anticancer agents that can selectively induce rapid apoptosis in malignant glioma cells.
the development of novel anticancer agents for malignant brain cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53p-Ante induces selective apoptosis of glioma cells through the Fas pathway and is a potential anticancer agent.
p53p-Ante is a promising new agent for selective induction of apoptosis in human and rodent gliomas, which may be delivered in vivo into the brain tumor by convection-enhanced technology.
the peptide p53p-A nt, which is derived from the COOH- terminal region of p53, can induce apoptosis in gliomas by a Fas-dependent mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a p53 COO-terminal peptide, p53p-A, induces rapid Fas-mediated apoptosis of glioma cells in vivo and in vitro.

the p53 COO terminal peptide, linked to the Antennapedia homeodomain, induces rapid apoptosis in glioma cells containing mutant or wild-type p53 and this peptide can be delivered into the tumor by a convective delivery system.

we have identified the mechanism for p53-induced apoptosis of glioma cells in vivo and in vitro and that this mechanism is Fas-mediated and that the p53 COOHTerminal peptide is able to induce apoptosis of glioma cell lines in vitro and in the brain tumor in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p53 COO-terminal peptide, p53p-A, is a unique and novel anticancer peptide that can induce selective Fas-mediated rapid apoptosis in human and rodent gliomas.
we have developed a novel anticancer agent that is highly selective for glioma cells and that it can be effectively delivered to the brain.
we have developed a novel anticancer agent, which is selective for malignant cells and nontoxic to normal proliferating cells.
